caseStudy.problem: The apartment had to earn and self-finance through guest stays. The initial two bedrooms were not enough for the demand, and every upgrade had to survive real check-ins, not only look good in a photoshoot.
caseStudy.decisions: The plan grew in phases over five years, from two bedrooms to four, while the home stayed open. Layout, materials, and styling were kept when guests and turnover proved them to be appropriate, and corrected when they did not. The space was designed for Jubili, the hospitality brand of this practice.
caseStudy.result: Superhost within the first six months, held since. Guest Favorite recognition. The same rooms that photograph well still work on ordinary turnover days.

work.name: Brabbeegasse
work.subtitle: Residential interior design and hospitality conversion
work.description: Designed for Jubili as the brand expanded to other properties. This project demonstrated that a rented space can be transformed to reflect a brand's aesthetic and also be returned to its original state once the leasing period ends, an important proof of concept for the reversibility of smart design interventions.

images.alt: Brabbeegasse, Vienna. blue room 1
Brabbeegasse, Vienna. blue room 6
Brabbeegasse, Vienna. kitchen 1

caseStudy.problem: The flat was leased. Guests wanted a more experiential stay, and the landlord still needed the space back in its original state when the lease ended.
caseStudy.decisions: Every finish and furniture move was planned to reverse. Paint, hardware, and freestanding pieces carried the look. Nothing that would leave a scar at handover.
caseStudy.result: A rental that reads as a finished guest home while it earns, and can be returned as found.

results.label: styled for stays, not only for photos
